claim: NASA's new Mars sample-return mission is launching in early 2026 and will bring back samples.
why: Mars Sample Return was restructured in 2025; launches moved to the 2030s and no 2026 launch exists.

claim: Bitcoin will reach $200K by 2025.
why: The 2025 deadline has passed; Bitcoin peaked near $126,000 in 2025.

claim: Humans will walk on Mars before 2040.
why: A prediction whose 2040 deadline has not passed cannot be checked yet, whatever the current outlook.

claim: Bitcoin will reach $500K by 2030.
why: Deadline in the future: unverifiable even though no evidence supports it today.

claim: Nvidia will be worth $10 trillion by 2028.
why: Deadline in the future.

claim: Asynchronous culture will become standard practice for remote teams.
why: Open-ended prediction with no deadline.

claim: Local offices might become optional hubs for remote-first companies.
why: Hedged, open-ended prediction.

claim: Remote-first companies will dominate talent acquisition in 2025 and beyond.
why: 2025 has passed and hybrid, not remote-first, is the most common arrangement; 'and beyond' keeps part of it open, so either verdict is defensible.

claim: The Perseverance rover landed in Jezero Crater in February 2021.
why: Landed February 18, 2021.

claim: The Mars samples were collected by the Perseverance rover.
why: Perseverance has been collecting and caching samples since 2021.

claim: Nvidia became the first company to hit a five trillion dollar market cap in 2025.
why: First to $5 trillion on October 29, 2025.

claim: Because the FDA reviews AI systems carefully, fully autonomous AI diagnostics are not happening anytime soon.
why: The FDA authorized IDx-DR, an autonomous AI diagnostic, in 2018.

claim: The FDA reviews AI-enabled medical devices before they reach patients.
why: The FDA reviews and lists more than 1,000 authorized AI-enabled devices.

claim: Some hospitals use AI for reading X-rays or flagging urgent cases.
why: Hospitals use AI triage on imaging, assisting clinicians.

claim: Hospitals offer triage chatbots that help patients decide next steps before seeing a doctor.
why: Symptom checkers and triage chatbots are offered online.

claim: The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digital health adoption.
why: Telehealth use stabilized far above pre-pandemic levels.

claim: AI trained on existing clinical data can inherit bias from that data.
why: Documented in Science (Obermeyer et al., 2019).

claim: GitLab is an all-remote company that publishes its handbook publicly.
why: GitLab's handbook is public.

claim: Automattic has been a fully distributed company since 2005.
why: Distributed since its founding in 2005.

claim: Hybrid is the most common arrangement for remote-capable US workers.
why: About half of remote-capable workers are hybrid.

claim: Venture capital funding dilutes founders' ownership and can bring pressure for exits.
why: Dilution and fund-lifecycle exit pressure are well documented.

claim: Bootstrapping trades growth speed for ownership and control.
why: Standard trade-off.

claim: Samir Gupta built a SaaS company with no outside capital that reached break-even in 18 months.
why: A personal anecdote with no public record.

claim: A fintech startup Emily Rogers advised raised a seed round and secured market leadership within two years.
why: Unnamed company; nothing specific to check.

claim: Emily Rogers has raised multiple funding rounds.
why: Personal history with no public record.
